verdict.rationale: Google's docs clearly cover using the key as a 2-Step Verification factor for Google accounts. They also make a generic claim that it works on 'other sites that support FIDO CTAP1 standards' and across work and personal services, and community reports confirm it works in Firefox on Linux without Google software. Missing for 10: any evidence naming GitHub, Microsoft, or password managers as supported services, explicit WebAuthn (not just CTAP1/U2F) documentation, and independent hands-on reports of it working on non-Google services.

support.subject: As a power user, the key works as a WebAuthn/U2F second factor across the major services I already use — Google, GitHub, Microsoft, password managers

citations.quote: Security keys can be used with 2-Step Verification to help you keep hackers out of your Google Account.
Along with Google and Google Cloud services, you can use Titan Security Keys on other sites that support FIDO CTAP1 standards.
One security key can be used to sign in to work and personal services.
Both work with Firefox on Linux, without any Google software.
